query: The Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic phases during solidification and exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence. Under rapid cooling, slower cooling, and subsequent reheating assessed by thermal analysis, what single intervention could increase amorphous retention and thermal stability while overcoming extensive primary crystallization? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted outcome relative to the alloy’s reported glass formation and crystallization behavior, the relevant cooling-rate and reheating boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Minor boron microalloying that partially substitutes phosphorus (e.g., Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P17B3, at.% balance unchanged) will increase amorphous retention during rapid and slower cooling and raise thermal stability upon reheating by suppressing extensive primary non-eutectic crystallization and delaying the multistep crystallization sequence.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast high-entropy/metalloid alloy nominally Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 (at.%) produced from high-purity elements, known to form multiple primary non-eutectic phases on solidification and to exhibit a multistep crystallization sequence upon reheating.
generation.intervention: Replace ~3 at.% of P with B to yield Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P17B3, with no other process changes.
generation.conditions: Solidification under identical melt-spinning or splat-quenching conditions as baseline (representative cooling rates: rapid ≥10^5 K/s; slower 10^3–10^4 K/s). Reheating by DSC at 5–20 K/min under high-purity Ar. Oxygen and nitrogen minimized (<100 ppm in melt) to avoid heterogeneous nucleation.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of mixed (P,B)-centered short-range order around transition metals (TM–(P,B) covalent-metallic clusters) that increases packing frustration, deepens the effective eutectic, and raises the melt viscosity near Tl, thereby elevating the reduced glass transition temperature (Trg = Tg/Tl) and suppressing nucleation of primary non-eutectic intermetallic phases.
generation.mechanism: Boron has strong negative mixing enthalpies with Cr/Fe/Ni/Co/Mn and a small atomic size, promoting dense TM–(P,B) networks. Partial P→B substitution lowers the effective liquidus and increases the nucleation barrier for primary phases by (i) enhancing chemical/size mismatch, (ii) increasing undercooled melt viscosity, and (iii) redirecting early-stage clustering away from the compositions of observed primary intermetallics. This reduces primary-phase selection during solidification and shifts the first crystallization event to higher temperature on reheating, simplifying or delaying the multistep sequence.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the reported behavior of the P20 alloy, the P17B3 variant will: (1) retain a larger amorphous fraction at the same cooling rate (qualitatively: less or no detectable primary intermetallics in XRD for rapid ≥10^5 K/s; for slower 10^3–10^4 K/s, a measurable reduction in crystalline volume fraction), and (2) exhibit increased thermal stability during reheating, with the onset of primary crystallization shifting upward by roughly 20–50 K and the first exotherm reduced in magnitude or merged to fewer events. The glass transition becomes more discernible and ΔTx (= Tx − Tg) increases modestly (on the order of tens of kelvin) under 5–20 K/min DSC.
generation.baseline: Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms several primary non-eutectic phases on solidification and shows a complex, multistep crystallization sequence on reheating. Even under rapid cooling, amorphous retention is limited by early primary crystallization; under slower cooling (10^3–10^4 K/s) primary phases dominate. DSC reveals multiple exotherms beginning near the onset of crystallization.
generation.boundary: The improvement is expected when cooling rates are ≥10^4 K/s; at ≤10^3 K/s, suppression of primary crystallization may be insufficient. If B exceeds ~5 at.% or oxygen is high (>200 ppm), boride formation or heterogeneous nucleation may reintroduce primary crystallization. At very high heating rates (>40 K/min), apparent Tx shifts may be kinetic and not reflect increased thermodynamic stability.
generation.uncertainty: Moderate: Exact magnitudes (amorphous fraction, Tg/Tx shifts, exotherm count) are uncertain because multicomponent interactions in this HEA–metalloid system can redirect phase selection. It is also uncertain whether boron introduces competitive boride nucleation at this specific composition without empirical calibration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two alloys from identical charges and processing: baseline Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 and boron-modified Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P17B3. Produce ribbons at controlled wheel speeds to target cooling rates of ~10^5 K/s (rapid) and ~10^3–10^4 K/s (slower). Characterize phase content and thermal response identically.
measurements: XRD (Cu Kα) to quantify amorphous vs crystalline fractions and identify primary phases in as-quenched ribbons at both cooling rates
TEM/SAED on as-quenched ribbons to detect nanocrystallites
DSC at 10 K/min (repeat at 5 and 20 K/min) to measure Tg, Tx, exotherm count and enthalpy
High-temperature XRD during reheating to track phase evolution
Chemical analysis (O/N, B, P contents) to ensure compositions and cleanliness match targets
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if, relative to the baseline alloy under the same processing and measurement conditions: (i) the boron-modified alloy does not show any increase in amorphous fraction (within ±5% absolute) at rapid cooling, and (ii) the onset of primary crystallization (Tx) does not increase by at least 20 K, or the multistep exotherm sequence is not reduced/delayed; observing new primary boride phases dominating as-quenched microstructures would also falsify the proposed mechanism.
